reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset, and Brown distinguish the idolatrous high places Asa destroyed from the sanctioned Yahweh high places he left standing, calling the reform incomplete.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen says the Chronicler both makes Asa 'another Josiah' who abolishes the high places and then mechanically repeats Kings' notice that they were not removed.

quotes.text: he even exaggerates this improvement, and makes of Asa another Josiah (2Chronicles xv. 1-15), represents him also (xiv. 3) as abolishing the high places, and yet after all … repeats the statement of 1Kings xv. 14 that the high places were not removed.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885 Eng. transl.), on 1 Kings 15:14 and 2 Chronicles 14:3-15:17.

sides.snippet: the high places were not taken away
sides.verseText: But the high places were not taken away: nevertheless the heart of Asa was perfect with Yahweh all his days.

sides.snippet: he took away out of all the cities of Judah the high places
sides.verseText: Also he took away out of all the cities of Judah the high places and the sun-images: and the kingdom was quiet before him.
